Google Drive backup

Backup folder

To use Google Drive backup, this app needs its own Google setup — one time only:

  1. Create a Google Cloud project.
  2. Set up the OAuth consent screen and add yourself as a test user.
  3. Enable the Google Drive API in that project.
  4. Create a Web OAuth client ID and add this app’s addresses to its authorized JavaScript origins.
  5. Create an API key in that project.

Then paste the client ID and API key into the two fields above — they are kept on this device only. You can also enter your Google account under “Google account” to have Log on go straight to that account instead of showing the account chooser.

My Drive

Information

The map

Height = chapters; each layer a chapter, each block a verse. Switch 2D/3D; drag to orbit, tap a book to open it.

Highlights

Pick a chapter, tap verses, tap the star — marked verses glow yellow and form your current set.

Search

References, text, or Strong's numbers; Show (N) paints the results.

Reading

English, Traditional Chinese, or Japanese. Tap a verse number to favorite it; words link to their Strong's entries.

Strong's

Definition plus every occurrence; steppers walk neighbouring numbers.

Collections

Tick sets and Load to render them combined; name + Save keeps a new one. Long-press a collection's name to rename it — the rename opens on its own page, clear of the keyboard. Export plain text copies the ticked collections, or all of them when none are ticked; import by pasting or from Google Drive.

Save shortcut

Appears above Search once any verse is marked; opens the save panel — save the staged verses as a collection, or switch to the Links tab to save them as a link set instead.

Favorites

Red marks your favorites; the heart in Controls loads all in red. Export/import on the Favorites tab.

Verse Notes

Long-press a verse number and choose Notes (or use the note icon on a verse page) to add a note; a white dot marks noted verses. Export/import on the Notes tab.

Links

Long-press a verse number and choose Links (or the link icon on a verse page) to tie verses together in a set of two or more; a purple dot marks linked verses, including in the chapter and verse pickers. A set's page can read the set or show it in purple — showing one set also joins its bricks with purple lines — and the Links button in Controls paints all the sets on the map at once, each in its own colour (a single set in purple). The Link lines button in Controls hides or shows a displayed set's joining lines. Export/import on the Links tab, which also lists every set: a set can be named when created or renamed later by long-pressing its name, which opens a rename page clear of the keyboard, and ticking Current selections or sets there lets you save them combined as a set or render them on the map, and Export plain text copies just the ticked sets — or every set when none are ticked. Any single-book rendering shows a round Links button on its right side when the book appears in a link set; tapping it renders just the sets that touch that book, and Back returns to the book.

Verse of the Day

On the home screen — tap to show its verse alone in the 3D view; a verse that is cut off expands first.

Reading plans

The calendar button at the bottom centre opens the Plans page: every loaded plan with its progress pie on the right of the card (projected vs actual — the days read in green, and when behind only the behind segment in red; under the percentage the pie shows the days to finish, always as a negative count of the days still to go (−364 just after a 365-day plan starts, rising to −1 when one day is left, and 0 once the plan is finished), green normally and red when behind; tapping the pie scrolls the day strip back to today), a day strip that scrolls sideways through every day of the plan — done days greyed, the current day in spring green — with the wide pill scroll bar under it, just the beginning and end dates joined by a dash, and on the left, where the pie used to sit, a round Zero out dial the same size as the pie: a clock with its twelve ticks on the pale ring band and a single needle, 3px thick at the base and tapering to a sharp point, that turns a tick a day — green and clockwise when you are ahead, red and counterclockwise when behind, going around again past twelve — with the +N or -N inside it under the needle, in the same green or red — moving above the centre instead whenever the needle would lie on top of it; one tap on the dial re-baselines a plan you have fallen behind on or run ahead of by moving only the projected end date, later or earlier, and the dial stays on the card afterwards, its needle resting at twelve in green while you are on schedule, with a small green thumbs-up where the count would sit; a day counts as behind only once it has fully passed, so the morning of a reading day never shows you behind before you have read; the beginning date is the day Day 1 was finished — a fact that never changes. Long-press the dial and confirm the Are you sure popup to mark every day up to the last day you have read as read, filling any gaps in between. A plan's start date is set the day you mark Day 1 done. Long-press the pie and confirm the Are you sure popup to reset a plan entirely — its start date is cleared and no days are read, ready for starting over. Plan progress is kept under a permanent storage key, the way the text-size setting is, so it carries across new builds of the app untouched. The day strip and the day preview list a day’s passages with abbreviated book names in the current display language, whichever language the plan’s own text uses. Tapping a day opens its passages on the search preview page, which wears spring green while you read a plan day; the preview’s Show button renders the day’s verses on the map in spring green with auto-circle and labels on, and the map’s back button returns to the day preview; after reading, mark the day done with the green check button on the preview — that is the only place a day is marked — and it brings you back to this page with the progress already updated. Import/export plans on the Plans tab of Import and Export — each plan is a file in the "plans" subfolder of your Drive backup folder. An imported plan whose name matches a built-in plan counts as already present: no duplicate is added, the built-in plan itself is left as it is, and any reading progress the import carries merges into the built-in plan's own progress. A tiny info button at the end of a plan’s name on this page, inline with the name text as if part of it, opens a popup with a brief description of the plan and its source; the description and source are part of the plan itself and travel with it through import and export — in the pasted text, the JSON, and the Drive plan files — and a plan imported with no source of its own keeps the place it was imported from as its source. A built-in “Bible in a year” plan is loaded by default — all 31,102 verses divided as evenly as possible over 365 days, with no lone verse of a book or chapter left at a day’s start or end — and like the built-in collection and link set it cannot be deleted and restores itself if missing. A second built-in plan, “Proverbs and Ecclesiastes”, keeps no dates and tracks nothing: each day it serves the Proverbs chapter matching the day of the month and the Ecclesiastes chapter matching the month, and its card shows three centred buttons — yesterday’s date, Today, and tomorrow’s date in month/day form, dates only with no reference on them — each opening that date’s serving; it has no file form, so it is never imported or exported as a file. On the Plans tab, a built-in plan’s delete button deactivates it instead — its row greys out and it leaves the Plans page — and the row’s Import button activates it again. Plans you import can be deleted from their row on the Plans tab, and an Are you sure popup asks before one is deleted.

Tours

Fly-through, car ride, and auto-circle — all in Controls.
